table_result.name: //bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/royston-dev-8253/datasets/cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy/tables/customers
table_result.overview: This table stores comprehensive information about individual customers. It captures key demographic and registration details for each customer. This data supports analysis of customer segmentation, regional distribution, and acquisition trends. It also facilitates understanding customer origins and geographic spread.

fields.name: city
fields.description: This column contains the city where the customer resides.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: This column holds a unique identifier for each customer.

fields.name: name
fields.description: This column contains the full name of the customer.

fields.name: segment
fields.description: This column stores the assigned segment for each customer.

fields.name: region
fields.description: This column holds the geographical region where the customer is located.

fields.name: signup_date
fields.description: This column contains the date when the customer registered.

fields.name: referred_by
fields.description: This column stores the identifier of the customer who referred the current customer.

fields.name: state
fields.description: This column contains the state where the customer resides.

queries.sql:
WITH ReferralCounts AS (
  SELECT
    referred_by AS referrer_customer_id,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS referred_count
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
  WHERE referred_by IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY referred_by
)
SELECT
  rc.referrer_customer_id,
  c.name AS referrer_name,
  rc.referred_count
FROM ReferralCounts AS rc
JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c
  ON rc.referrer_customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE rc.referred_count > (
  SELECT
    APPROX_QUANTILES(referred_count, 100)[OFFSET(99)]
  FROM ReferralCounts
)
ORDER BY rc.referred_count DESC;
queries.description: Find customers who were referred by an unusually high number of other customers, indicating potential referral fraud or a highly influential customer, by identifying those in the top 1% of referrers.

queries.sql:
WITH RegionalSignupStats AS (
  SELECT
    region,
    AVG(UNIX_DATE(signup_date)) AS avg_signup_unix_date,
    STDDEV(UNIX_DATE(signup_date)) AS stddev_signup_unix_date
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.name,
  c.region,
  c.signup_date,
  DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(CAST(rs.avg_signup_unix_date AS INT64))) AS average_regional_signup_date,
  ABS(UNIX_DATE(c.signup_date) - rs.avg_signup_unix_date) AS days_from_average
FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c
JOIN RegionalSignupStats AS rs
  ON c.region = rs.region
WHERE ABS(UNIX_DATE(c.signup_date) - rs.avg_signup_unix_date) > (3 * rs.stddev_signup_unix_date)
ORDER BY days_from_average DESC;
queries.description: Identify customers who signed up on dates that are significantly outside the typical signup patterns for their respective regions, defined by a 3-standard-deviation threshold from the regional average signup date.

queries.sql: SELECT region, CORR(customer_count, avg_signup_date_days) AS customer_signup_date_correlation FROM (SELECT region, city, COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count, AVG(UNIX_DATE(signup_date)) AS avg_signup_date_days FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` GROUP BY region, city) GROUP BY region;
queries.description: Calculate the correlation between the number of customers in a city and the average signup date (represented as days since a fixed epoch) for that city, within each region.

queries.sql: SELECT region, (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) BETWEEN 7 AND 12 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS growth_rate FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` WHERE referred_by IS NOT NULL GROUP BY region HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) BETWEEN 1 AND 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 ORDER BY growth_rate DESC LIMIT 5;
queries.description: Find the top 5 regions with the highest growth rate in customer sign-ups between the first and second half of the year, considering only customers who were referred.

queries.sql: SELECT state FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` WHERE signup_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 YEAR) GROUP BY state ORDER BY COUNT(CASE WHEN referred_by IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(CASE WHEN referred_by IS NULL THEN 1 END) DESC LIMIT 1;
queries.description: Find the state with the highest ratio of referred customers to non-referred customers, considering only customers who signed up in the last two years.

queries.sql:
WITH OverallSignupStats AS (
  SELECT
    AVG(UNIX_DATE(signup_date)) AS overall_avg_signup_unix_date,
    STDDEV(UNIX_DATE(signup_date)) AS overall_stddev_signup_unix_date
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
),
SegmentSignupStats AS (
  SELECT
    segment,
    AVG(UNIX_DATE(signup_date)) AS segment_avg_signup_unix_date
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
  GROUP BY segment
)
SELECT
  sss.segment,
  DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(CAST(sss.segment_avg_signup_unix_date AS INT64))) AS segment_average_signup_date,
  DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(CAST(oss.overall_avg_signup_unix_date AS INT64))) AS overall_average_signup_date,
  ABS(sss.segment_avg_signup_unix_date - oss.overall_avg_signup_unix_date) AS days_difference
FROM SegmentSignupStats AS sss
CROSS JOIN OverallSignupStats AS oss
WHERE ABS(sss.segment_avg_signup_unix_date - oss.overall_avg_signup_unix_date) > (2 * oss.overall_stddev_signup_unix_date)
ORDER BY days_difference DESC;
queries.description: Identify customer segments that have a significantly lower or higher average signup date compared to the overall average signup date across all customers, using a 2-standard-deviation threshold.

queries.sql: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(CASE WHEN c.region != r.region THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(c.customer_id) AS cross_region_referral_percentage FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c LEFT JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS r ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;
queries.description: For each customer segment, calculate the percentage of customers who were referred by someone from a different region.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  CORR(c1.customer_id, c2.customer_id) AS customer_id_referral_correlation
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c1
JOIN
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c2
ON
  c1.referred_by = c2.customer_id;
queries.description: Calculate the correlation between a customer's `customer_id` and the `customer_id` of the person who referred them, to see if there's any numerical relationship in referral chains.

queries.sql: SELECT c.region, AVG(DATE_DIFF(c.signup_date, r.signup_date, DAY)) AS avg_referral_signup_gap_days FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS r ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.region;
queries.description: Calculate the average number of days between a customer's signup date and the signup date of the customer who referred them, broken down by region.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  region,
  LOGICAL_OR(segment = 'Premium') AS has_premium_segment
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
GROUP BY
  region
HAVING
  LOGICAL_OR(segment = 'Premium')
ORDER BY
  region;
queries.description: Identify regions where the logical OR of all customer segments being 'Premium' is true, indicating regions with a significant presence of premium customers.

queries.sql: SELECT region FROM (SELECT region, state, COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` GROUP BY region, state) GROUP BY region ORDER BY STDDEV(customer_count) DESC LIMIT 1;
queries.description: Find the region with the highest standard deviation in the number of customers per state.

queries.sql: SELECT state, city, referred_customer_percentage FROM (SELECT state, city, COUNT(CASE WHEN referred_by IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(customer_id) AS referred_customer_percentage, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY COUNT(CASE WHEN referred_by IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(customer_id) DESC) AS rn FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` GROUP BY state, city) WHERE rn <= 3;
queries.description: Identify the top 3 cities within each state that have the highest percentage of customers referred by another customer.

queries.sql:
WITH MonthlySignups AS (
  SELECT
    FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', signup_date) AS signup_month,
    region,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS monthly_signups
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
  WHERE signup_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT
  signup_month,
  region,
  monthly_signups,
  LAG(monthly_signups, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY signup_month) AS previous_month_signups,
  (monthly_signups - LAG(monthly_signups, 1, 0) OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY signup_month)) AS signup_difference
FROM MonthlySignups
ORDER BY signup_month, region;
queries.description: Analyze the monthly customer signup trends by region, comparing the current month's signups to the previous month's signups.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  region,
  ANY_VALUE(city) AS city_with_most_segments,
  COUNT(DISTINCT segment) AS distinct_segments_count
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
GROUP BY
  region, city
QUALIFY
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT segment) DESC) = 1
ORDER BY
  region;
queries.description: Find the city within each region that has the most distinct customer segments, indicating diverse customer bases.

queries.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(r.customer_id) AS referral_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS r ON c.customer_id = r.referred_by GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY referral_count DESC LIMIT 1;
queries.description: Identify the customer who has referred the most other customers, and list their name and the count of their referrals.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  signup_date,
  segment,
  COUNT(customer_id) AS daily_signups,
  SUM(COUNT(customer_id)) OVER (PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY signup_date) AS cumulative_signups
FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
WHERE signup_date BETWEEN DATE_TRUNC(CURRENT_DATE(), YEAR) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY signup_date, segment
ORDER BY segment, signup_date;
queries.description: Calculate the cumulative number of customer signups over time for each customer segment, showing the running total of new customers.

queries.sql:
WITH StateSignups AS (
  SELECT
    region,
    state,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS state_signup_count,
    SUM(COUNT(customer_id)) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_total_signups
  FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE())
  GROUP BY region, state
),
RankedStateSignups AS (
  SELECT
    region,
    state,
    state_signup_count,
    region_total_signups,
    (state_signup_count * 100.0 / region_total_signups) AS percentage_of_region_signups,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY state_signup_count DESC) AS rank_in_region
  FROM StateSignups
)
SELECT
  region,
  state,
  state_signup_count,
  percentage_of_region_signups
FROM RankedStateSignups
WHERE rank_in_region <= 3
ORDER BY region, rank_in_region;
queries.description: Identify the top 3 states within each region with the highest number of customer signups for the current year, including the percentage of signups they represent within their region.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  VAR_SAMP(referral_count) AS variance_of_referral_counts
FROM (
  SELECT
    referred_by,
    COUNT(customer_id) AS referral_count
  FROM
    `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
  WHERE
    referred_by IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    referred_by
  HAVING
    COUNT(customer_id) > 0
);
queries.description: Calculate the sample variance of the number of customers each customer has referred, for customers who have referred at least one person.

queries.sql: SELECT region, AVG(customer_count) AS average_customers_per_city FROM (SELECT region, city, COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` GROUP BY region, city HAVING COUNT(customer_id) > 10) GROUP BY region;
queries.description: Calculate the average number of customers per city for each region, but only for cities with more than 10 customers.

queries.sql: SELECT region, APPROX_QUANTILES(UNIX_DATE(signup_date), 100)[OFFSET(90)] AS ninetieth_percentile_signup_date FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` WHERE SUBSTR(name, 1, 1) IN ('A', 'E', 'I', 'O', 'U', 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u') GROUP BY region;
queries.description: Calculate the 90th percentile of customer signup dates (in days since epoch) for each region, considering only customers whose names start with a vowel.

queries.sql: SELECT segment, APPROX_QUANTILES(UNIX_DATE(signup_date), 2)[OFFSET(1)] AS median_signup_date_unix FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` WHERE signup_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) GROUP BY segment;
queries.description: Determine the median signup date for customers in each segment, considering only customers who signed up in the last year.

queries.sql: SELECT state, COUNT(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM signup_date) = 1 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(customer_id) AS first_quarter_signup_percentage FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` GROUP BY state;
queries.description: Determine the percentage of customers in each state who signed up in the first quarter of any year.

queries.sql: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(CASE WHEN c.city = r.city AND c.state != r.state THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(c.customer_id) AS same_city_different_state_referral_percentage FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS r ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;
queries.description: Determine the percentage of customers in each segment who were referred by someone from the same city, but a different state.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  state,
  STDDEV_SAMP(customer_id) AS customer_id_stddev
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
GROUP BY
  state
HAVING
  COUNT(customer_id) > 5
ORDER BY
  customer_id_stddev DESC;
queries.description: Determine the standard deviation of customer IDs within each state, considering only states with more than 5 customers, to identify states with highly varied customer ID distributions.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  region,
  ANY_VALUE(customer_id HAVING MIN signup_date) AS earliest_customer_id,
  MIN(signup_date) AS earliest_signup_date,
  ANY_VALUE(customer_id HAVING MAX signup_date) AS latest_customer_id,
  MAX(signup_date) AS latest_signup_date
FROM
  `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers`
GROUP BY
  region
ORDER BY
  region;
queries.description: For each region, find the customer ID of the customer who signed up earliest and the customer ID of the customer who signed up latest, along with their respective signup dates.

queries.sql:
SELECT
  c.region,
  AVG(DATE_DIFF(c.signup_date, r.signup_date, DAY)) AS avg_referral_time_difference_days
FROM `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS c
JOIN `royston-dev-8253.cymbal_bank_v6z_scaffold_demo_copy.customers` AS r
  ON c.referred_by = r.customer_id
WHERE c.signup_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 2 YEAR) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY c.region;
queries.description: Determine the average time difference in days between a customer's signup date and the signup date of the customer who referred them, grouped by the customer's region.
